lessons.title: How I Optimized My LinkedIn Profile and Got 20+ Interview Calls
objectives: Identify what actually produces inbound interest
Set a realistic expectation of how long it takes
lessons.notes:
Take the number in the title as marketing. It is one person, one field, one moment, and it says nothing about what you will get. Watch it for the mechanism rather than the result.

WHAT GENUINELY PRODUCES INBOUND INTEREST, in order of effect:
BEING SEARCHABLE FOR THE RIGHT TITLE, which is the headline, skills and role descriptions from Module 5. Without this nothing else matters, because you never appear.
LOCATION AND OPENNESS SET CORRECTLY, because these are hard filters that silently exclude people.
A COMPLETE PROFILE, since incomplete ones rank poorly.
EVIDENCE - something to look at, which turns a maybe into a message.
ACTIVITY, modestly. Being occasionally visible keeps you in view; posting constantly is not required and mostly does not help.
CONNECTIONS IN YOUR FIELD, because search results are influenced by network proximity and a profile connected to nobody in your industry surfaces less.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK: buying connections, engagement pods, posting daily to no purpose, and a profile that reads as a personal advertisement rather than a record of what you can do.

EXPECT MONTHS, NOT DAYS. A profile fixed today changes what searches you appear in, and then you wait for someone to run one.

MEASURE THE RIGHT THING: not views, but whether the right kind of person is looking. Ten views from recruiters in your field beats four hundred from strangers.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - the honest expectation from here, which no such video gives. INBOUND RECRUITER INTEREST IS MUCH THINNER IN THIS MARKET than these videos imply, because fewer local employers recruit that way. Fixing your profile is worth doing and it is not a strategy on its own - it makes you findable and credible when someone checks you, which they will. The applications you send and the people who know you remain the main channel. Second, WHERE THE PROFILE REALLY EARNS ITS KEEP IS REMOTE AND INTERNATIONAL WORK, so if that is your target, set location and remote availability carefully and connect deliberately with people in that field abroad. Third, BE ALERT TO FAKE RECRUITERS, which are common: a legitimate employer never asks you to pay for a job, a placement, training or a medical, and an offer arriving with no interview and a request for money is a fraud every time.
lessons.practice: Fix the searchable parts first - headline, skills, role descriptions, location, open-to-work - then check weekly for a month who is viewing your profile and whether they are in your field. Connect with twenty people who genuinely work in the job you want. Write down what actually produced any contact you received.

quiz.question: What must be right before anything else on a profile?
options: Being searchable for the right title, since otherwise you never appear

quiz.question: What is always a fraud?
options: An offer arriving with no interview and a request for money

lessons.title: Get Clients On Repeat: 5 Keys To Build A Freelance Personal Brand
objectives: Position yourself for one kind of work
Build the proof that makes a stranger trust you
lessons.notes:
Freelance branding is not a logo. It is being the person someone thinks of when a particular problem appears.

THE FIVE THINGS THAT ACTUALLY MATTER:
BE SPECIFIC. A freelancer who does everything is hired for nothing. I design and manage social media for restaurants is a position; I am a creative professional is not. Narrow does not mean fewer clients - it means being the obvious choice for the ones you want.
SHOW THE WORK. Not a description of your skills, the work itself, with what the client wanted and what changed. Three real pieces beat any amount of description.
BE CONSISTENTLY REACHABLE. Answering within the day, saying when you will deliver and delivering then. Unreliability loses more freelance income here than lack of skill, by a wide margin.
BE VISIBLE WHERE THE WORK IS. Not everywhere - in the one or two places your clients actually are.
ASK FOR THE REFERRAL. Satisfied clients recommend you when prompted and rarely think to otherwise.

REPEAT WORK IS THE WHOLE GAME. Finding a new client costs several times what keeping one does, so the end of a job is the start of the next: ask what else is difficult, suggest the obvious next thing, and check in later.

SAY NO to work outside your position. Taking everything is how you end up with no reputation for anything.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - how this works in practice here. YOUR BRAND IS YOUR WHATSAPP AND YOUR WORD OF MOUTH, far more than any profile. Keep a business number, reply properly, use a clear display name and photograph, and keep an album of your work you can send in thirty seconds - that album wins more jobs here than a portfolio site. Second, RELIABILITY IS THE POSITION. In a market where a great many people disappear mid-job, being the freelancer who answers, delivers on the day promised, and says so when something slips is itself a competitive advantage, and it is the thing clients describe when they recommend you. Third, TAKE A DEPOSIT AND WRITE THE SCOPE IN THE CHAT - it is not distrust, it is professionalism, and clients who balk at a deposit are usually the ones who would not have paid the balance.
lessons.practice: Write your position in one sentence naming what you do and who for, and remove from your profiles everything that contradicts it. Assemble a work album you can send in thirty seconds. Then contact three past clients or people you have done work for, ask what else is difficult, and ask each for one referral.

quiz.question: Why be specific about what you do?
options: A freelancer who does everything is hired for nothing
Specialists can charge by the hour

quiz.question: What loses more freelance income here than lack of skill?
options: Unreliability - not answering, not delivering when promised

lessons.title: 10 Easy Steps to Tailor Your Resume to Any Job Description
objectives: Decide what to cut as well as what to add
Apply at a pace that produces interviews
lessons.notes:
This is the applied lesson. Take three real adverts for jobs you would actually accept and work them properly.

THE PROCESS, and it should take fifteen minutes once practised:
1. READ THE ADVERT TWICE. Mark hard requirements, named tools, and repeated words.
2. WORK OUT WHAT THE JOB IS REALLY FOR - what problem they are hiring to solve. It is usually visible between the lines and it tells you what to emphasise.
3. REWRITE THE TOP SUMMARY for this role specifically. This is the highest-value two minutes.
4. REORDER EXPERIENCE so the relevant sits first.
5. REWRITE THREE OR FOUR BULLETS to face this job, using their vocabulary where it is true.
6. CUT what does not serve this application. Cutting is as important as adding and nobody does it.
7. MATCH THE SKILLS LIST to what they named, honestly.
8. CHECK EVERY CLAIM survives five minutes of questioning.
9. NAME THE FILE with your name and the role.
10. READ IT ALOUD once. Errors you cannot see, you hear.

TRACK YOUR APPLICATIONS: where, when, the version sent, and the outcome. After thirty applications the record tells you whether the problem is your CV, the roles you choose, or the volume - and nobody tracks this, so everybody guesses.

IF YOU ARE GETTING NO REPLIES AT ALL, the problem is usually the fit of the roles or the top third of the document, not the fine detail further down.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - the realities of applying here. MANY GOOD ROLES ARE NEVER ADVERTISED, so applications alone are half a strategy; the other half is telling people specifically what you are looking for, which the personal branding lesson covered. Second, FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS EXACTLY - the subject line they asked for, the documents they listed, the deadline - because local shortlisting often starts by discarding everything that ignored the instructions, and that is the cheapest filter an employer has. Third, APPLY EARLY: many employers here review as applications arrive rather than after the closing date, so the first week matters more than the last day. And keep your certificates, identification and good conduct certificate scanned and ready, so a two-day deadline is not the thing that stops you.
lessons.practice: Tailor your CV to three real adverts in fifteen minutes each, cutting as much as you add, and follow every instruction in the advert exactly. Start an application record with where, when, version and outcome. Then send all three within a week of the advert appearing.

quiz.question: What does everybody skip when tailoring?
options: Cutting what does not serve this application

quiz.question: Why does the first week after an advert appears matter most?
options: Many employers here review applications as they arrive rather than after the deadline

lessons.title: How to Optimize Your LinkedIn Profile — Complete Guide
objectives: Rebuild a full profile section by section
Write an About section that is read
lessons.notes:
This is the full rebuild. Work through it with your profile open and finish it in one sitting - a half-rebuilt profile is worse than the old one.

SECTION BY SECTION:
PHOTOGRAPH - your face, clear, daylight, plain background, friendly. It does not need a photographer.
BANNER - a simple image related to your field. Low effort, and its absence reads as an abandoned profile.
HEADLINE - the three-part formula from Module 5.
ABOUT - write it as a person speaking, in the first person. What you do, who you do it for, what you are good at, and what you are looking for. Three short paragraphs. The first two lines are what shows before anyone clicks more, so put the substance there.
EXPERIENCE - real titles, and descriptions with outcomes and the tools you used. Not copied from your CV word for word; slightly more human.
SKILLS - the words that would be filtered on, ordered with the most important first.
EDUCATION, certifications, and anything you have built.
FEATURED - put your actual work here if you have anything showable. It is the most underused section on the platform.

RECOMMENDATIONS ARE WORTH REAL EFFORT. Three specific ones from people who supervised or worked with you beat twenty endorsements. Ask directly, remind them what you worked on together, and offer to write one back - most people are willing and simply need prompting.

KEEP IT CURRENT. A profile last updated three years ago says something you did not intend.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - three things for this market. WRITE THE ABOUT SECTION SO IT MAKES SENSE TO SOMEONE WHO DOES NOT KNOW KENYAN INSTITUTIONS: name what the organisation does rather than assuming its name carries meaning, because a recruiter abroad reading a list of unfamiliar employers learns nothing. Second, MAKE YOUR CONTACT DETAILS USABLE - an email you actually check and, if you are open to it, a phone number, because a recruiter who cannot reach you outside the platform often does not try. Third, ASK FOR RECOMMENDATIONS WHILE PEOPLE STILL REMEMBER YOU, not a year after leaving - a supervisor from an attachment or a short contract will write a good one the week you finish and will struggle to a year later.
lessons.practice: Rebuild every section in one sitting, ending with the About section written in the first person with the substance in the first two lines. Add at least one item to Featured. Then ask three people who actually supervised or worked with you for a recommendation, reminding each what you worked on together.

quiz.question: Which section is most underused?
options: Featured, where your actual work can be shown

quiz.question: Why describe what an employer does rather than just naming it?
options: A recruiter abroad learns nothing from a list of unfamiliar organisation names
It is required by the platform

lessons.title: How Does a Resume Writer Accept New Clients?
objectives: Run a CV writing service as a defined process
Gather what you need from a client efficiently
Deliver something the client can use and maintain
lessons.notes:
CV writing is a real service with steady demand, and the skill being sold is not writing - it is asking the right questions and knowing what an employer responds to.

THE PROCESS:
THE INTAKE. You cannot write a good CV from a bad one. Ask for the existing document, the kind of role they want, two or three adverts they would apply to, and then a conversation - what they actually did, what changed because of it, what they are proud of. That conversation is where the material comes from, because clients consistently omit their best work.
THE DRAFT, built from the target roles rather than from their history.
ONE REVISION ROUND, stated in advance.
THE HANDOVER: the document in an editable format and a PDF, plus a short note on how to tailor it for each application, because a client who cannot adapt it is back in a month expecting free work.

WHAT TO OFFER BEYOND THE CV: a LinkedIn rewrite, a cover letter template, and interview preparation. These are natural additions and they are usually the more profitable half.

MANAGE EXPECTATIONS EXPLICITLY. You are selling a better document, not a job. Say so in writing, kindly and plainly, because a client who believed otherwise is an unhappy client however good your work was.

BE HONEST ABOUT WHAT A CV CANNOT FIX: a genuine lack of the required qualification, or applying to roles far beyond current experience. Telling someone that is more useful than a beautifully written document that will not work.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - the shape of this service here. ASK FIRST WHETHER THEY ARE APPLYING LOCALLY OR ABROAD, and deliver the right document - the two-page local CV with referees, or the one-page international resume with no photograph or personal details - and where they are doing both, deliver both and explain when to use each. That single question is what makes you visibly better than the person charging half your price. Second, MOST CLIENTS WILL SEND YOU EVERYTHING ON WHATSAPP as photographs, so build an intake form of ten questions they can answer as voice notes or text, because it gets you better material than asking them to write. Third, HANDLE THEIR DOCUMENTS CAREFULLY: you will be sent identification, certificates and personal details, which are valuable to a fraudster - keep them somewhere access-controlled, never in a shared gallery, and delete them when the job is done, saying so to the client.
lessons.practice: Write your intake: the ten questions you will ask, answerable by voice note. Then write one CV for a real person start to finish, asking first whether they are applying locally or abroad and delivering the right version. Include the short note on how to tailor it, and write your expectations paragraph saying what you do and do not promise.

quiz.question: Where does the material for a good CV come from?
options: The intake conversation, because clients consistently omit their best work

quiz.question: What single question makes a CV writer visibly better here?
options: Whether they are applying locally or abroad, since the two documents differ

lessons.title: Freelance Pricing Strategies: How to Charge What You're Worth
objectives: Price by the package rather than by the hour
Set a floor and hold it
Handle the price conversation without discounting reflexively
lessons.notes:
Pricing is where most freelancers here lose money, and the cause is almost always the same: quoting a number quickly to avoid an uncomfortable moment.

PRICE THE PACKAGE, NOT THE HOUR. A client buys a finished CV, a rebuilt profile, a set of applications they can send. Hourly pricing punishes you as you get faster, and you will get much faster.

BUILD PACKAGES AT THREE LEVELS: a CV only; a CV with LinkedIn and a cover letter; and the full service including interview preparation. Most people choose the middle one, which is the point of having three.

COUNT EVERYTHING before you name a number: the intake conversation, the writing, the revision, the messages, and the follow-up questions that arrive for weeks afterwards. Beginners count only the writing.

SET A FLOOR from what you need each month divided by the clients you can genuinely serve, and do not quote below it. Work taken below your floor is done resentfully and becomes the price you are known for.

WHEN THEY SAY IT IS TOO EXPENSIVE: do not immediately drop the price. Ask what they were expecting, and either explain what is included or offer a smaller package - reducing the scope rather than the rate. A discount given without reducing the work teaches the client what your prices really are.

RAISE PRICES FOR NEW CLIENTS as you improve. Existing clients keep the old rate for a while; that is a courtesy, not a rule.

ADDITION BEYOND THE VIDEO - the terms that decide whether you are actually paid. TAKE FIFTY PER CENT BEFORE YOU START and the balance before the final files are handed over, on M-Pesa, with the scope and the revision limit written in the WhatsApp thread - that thread is your contract and it has settled arguments. STATE THE REVISION LIMIT explicitly, because a CV attracts opinions from the client's whole family and unlimited revisions turn a fair price into a bad one. Second, EXPECT THE PRICE OBJECTION AND DO NOT TAKE IT PERSONALLY - a real constraint is not an insult, and the right answer is a smaller package rather than the same work for less. Third, BE CAREFUL WITH PAY-WHEN-I-GET-THE-JOB, which people will propose: refuse it, kindly. You do not control whether they are hired, the timeline is unbounded, and you would be carrying the cost of their job search. Say that plainly and offer the small package instead.
lessons.practice: Build three packages with exactly what is included in each, the revision limit and the payment terms. List every task in one full job and estimate the hours honestly, then calculate your floor and check the middle package clears it. Write the sentence you will use when someone says it is too expensive, and the one for pay-when-I-get-the-job.

quiz.question: What should you do when a client says the price is too expensive?
options: Ask what they expected, then offer a smaller package rather than a discount
Reduce the price to keep the client

quiz.question: Why refuse pay-when-I-get-the-job?
options: You do not control the hiring, the timeline is unbounded, and you would fund their job search
